types.name: FormulaNode
types.doc: A score formula as the builder exports it (contract 17.1): a tree, never text. A `ref` is the block id of a question within the group's reach. Evaluated exactly as structured.

types.name: Score
types.doc: One score on a group (contract 17.1): a formula over the questions within the group's reach, calculated once per context the group appears in.

members.name: id
members.doc: Code pattern (contract 13.2); unique within this group's scores.

members.name: unanswered
members.doc: "no-score": any unanswered question leaves the score without a value. "zero": an unanswered question counts as 0 (contract 17.3).

members.name: decimals
members.doc: Whole number 0–4; default 0. Only the final result is rounded, half away from zero.

members.name: showToRespondent
members.doc: Listed for the respondent after a successful submit. Default false.

types.name: ScoreResult
types.doc: One calculated score (contract 17.5). `path` runs to the group as ValidationError.path does, ending with the instance position for a repeating group, e.g. ["patients", 1].

members.name: reason
members.doc: Present only when value is null.

types.name: calculateScores
types.text: function calculateScores(schema: FormSchema, answers: Answers): ScoreResult[];
types.doc: Every score in the form (contract section 17), calculated from `answers`. A score is calculated once for each context its group appears in: once for a group outside any repeat, once per instance of a repeating group, and once per enclosing instance for a plain group inside a repeat. A group that is hidden there, and a repeating group with no instances, give nothing. "Hidden" and "unanswered" mean exactly what they mean for validation and the payload filter: the same visibility, resolved per instance, and the same built-in checks. Results follow the form's reading order instance by instance — the order validation errors and the error summary use — and each context lists its group's scores in `scores` order (contract 17.5). Meant for answers that pass validateSubmission: prepareSubmission calls it only then, and so does the renderer, after a successful submit. A value that fails its built-in checks counts as unanswered; this never throws on answers. A schema that fails the integrity check throws, as everywhere in /core.
